title: Quiz: What Is a Statistical Model?

questions.text: In the decomposition y = f(x) + ε, what does ε represent?
options: The systematic pattern we want to learn
The random, irreducible noise that no model can explain
The fitted coefficient estimated from data
The residual computed after fitting the model
questions.explanation: ε is the noise component — random variation that is unpredictable and cannot be reduced by any model. f(x) is the signal. The residual eᵢ = yᵢ − ŷᵢ is an estimate of ε for each observation.

questions.text: The model family y = β₀ + β₁x and the fitted model ŷ = 0.25 + 0.77x are the same thing.
questions.explanation: They are distinct. The model family is the shape — all possible straight lines. The fitted model is the specific member of that family (with particular numbers for the intercept and slope) that was estimated from the data.

questions.text: You fit a linear model to the diamonds dataset and plot residuals vs carat. The residuals fan outward: small for low-carat diamonds and large for high-carat diamonds. What does this indicate?
options: The model is correctly specified and needs no refinement
There are no outliers in the dataset
The variance of the residuals increases with carat — heteroscedasticity
The relationship between price and carat is perfectly linear
questions.explanation: A fan shape in the residual plot is the signature of heteroscedasticity: the noise variance is not constant but grows with the predictor. This violates a key OLS assumption and suggests a variance-stabilising transformation (like log) is needed.

questions.text: In R, which function from the modelr package attaches the column 'resid' (eᵢ = yᵢ − ŷᵢ) to a data frame?
questions.explanation: add_residuals(model) computes eᵢ = yᵢ − ŷᵢ for every row in the data frame and appends it as a new column called 'resid'. add_predictions() appends fitted values instead.

questions.text: You fit lm(price ~ carat) and inspect the residuals. You notice that residuals cluster by cut level — all 'Fair' cut diamonds have negative residuals and all 'Ideal' diamonds have positive residuals. What should you conclude?
options: The model is well specified; clusters are just sampling noise
Cut is an irrelevant variable and should be excluded
The model is missing 'cut' as a predictor — it explains systematic variation in residuals
The residuals are correctly distributed around zero
questions.explanation: Systematic patterns in residuals — especially grouping by a variable not in the model — indicate that the variable is explaining variance that the model missed. Adding 'cut' as a predictor would reduce the residual variance and improve the model.

questions.text: In the iterative modelling cycle, we stop refining the model as soon as R² exceeds 0.80.
questions.explanation: We stop when residuals look like random noise — no systematic patterns remain. R² is one indicator of fit, but a model with R² = 0.80 can still have strongly patterned residuals, meaning it is missing important structure. Conversely, R² = 0.95 can coexist with well-behaved residuals. Residual inspection is the deciding criterion.
